title: When the Landfall Burns
premise: When a government survey team vanishes on the Vessin River, salvage captain Sable Amberdale is the only pilot willing to run the flooded upper reaches to find them. She discovers instead that the team was hunting a sunken revenue cutter full of stolen settlement funds, and that the survey's own leader staged the disappearance to claim it. Racing a rival salvage fleet and the dying dry season, Sable must choose between the fortune that could buy her freedom from the river and the justice the law will never deliver. In the end she scuttles the cutter's hold in deep water, gives the evidence to the families the money was stolen from, and finally admits the river — not the miles — is where she belongs.
about_author: Ines Fairweather spent a decade working seasonal river charters before turning to fiction, and her prose carries the salt-and-mud texture of that life. She writes adventure stories about people who find home in transit.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Sable, POV: loading cargo at Corlow Landing, she learns a survey team has vanished upstream and officials want a pilot fool enough to run the flood. Her first mate Tam urges refusal; debt and restlessness say otherwise. Beat: restless unease, the itch of miles not yet traveled.

chapters.title: The Contract
chapters.summary: Sable, POV: she signs with Inspector Halloway, cold and precise, who offers triple pay and asks oddly specific questions about sandbars near Cutter Bend. Tam warns the contract smells of salvage, not rescue. Beat: suspicion masked as ambition.

chapters.title: Running the Flood
chapters.summary: Sable, POV: the ascent upriver through churning water showcases her mastery; a near-capsize at Widow's Tooth proves why no one else would take the job. Crew trust deepens. Beat: exhilaration shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Gear and No Tracks
chapters.summary: Sable, POV: they reach the abandoned camp — tents pitched, kettle still warm, instruments left behind, no footprints leaving. Halloway searches too carefully for a man looking for survivors. Beat: creeping wrongness.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Tam, POV: diving at Cutter Bend, Tam finds a brass plate from the revenue cutter Vessel's Grace, sunk forty years ago with stolen settlement funds aboard. He hides it from Halloway. Beat: loyalty tested by temptation.

chapters.title: The Rival Fleet
chapters.summary: Sable, POV: smoke downstream — the Brannigan salvage fleet, three boats heavy with divers and winches, entering the reach. Their captain, Odile Brannigan, hails Sable with old familiarity and old debts. Beat: the race becomes real.

chapters.title: Halloway's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable, POV: snooping in Halloway's cabin, Sable finds his true orders: recover the funds quietly, list the surveyors as drowned. The vanishing was staged by someone inside the team. Beat: betrayal crystallizes into purpose.

chapters.title: The Sixth Man
chapters.summary: New character Juno Pell, POV: the survey's cartographer, hiding in a fisher's stilt-house, reveals leader Aldous Vane faked the disappearances to claim the wreck for himself and killed their radio operator. Beat: fear becoming resolve.

chapters.title: Tide Against Tide
chapters.summary: Sable, POV: Sable races Brannigan's fleet through a narrowing channel, using a hidden cut only she knows to leapfrog them. Brannigan reads the move and smiles — she knows this river too. Beat: fierce joy in competition.

chapters.title: Dry Season Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Tam, POV: water levels drop faster than charts predicted; six tides becomes four. The crew debates turning back versus pushing into channels that will strand them. Beat: the cost of commitment made concrete.

chapters.title: Old Debts
chapters.summary: Sable and Odile, alternating POV: moored overnight at the same bend, the two captains trade history over rum — Odile once saved Sable from a wreck, Sable once let Odile take the blame for smuggling. Uneasy truce forms. Beat: belonging found in an adversary.

chapters.title: Vane's Signal
chapters.summary: Juno, POV: Vane contacts Juno through a dead-drop, offering her a share to stay silent and revealing he knows Sable carries Halloway's secret orders. Juno must decide whom to warn. Beat: isolation and choice.

chapters.title: The Cut Closes
chapters.summary: Sable, POV: Vane's men sabotage the channel marker; Sable's boat grounds hard on a shifting bar, hull breached, two tides lost. Tam is injured. Beat: despair, the river turning hostile.

chapters.title: Careening
chapters.summary: Tam, POV: the crew careens the boat on a mudflat to patch her, working against the falling water. Odile arrives — and instead of claiming victory, lends hands and pumps. Beat: unexpected grace between rivals.

chapters.title: What Vane Found
chapters.summary: Juno, POV: scouting ahead, Juno sees Vane's camp at the wreck site, divers already down, and witnesses him order a diver sealed in the hold when the man threatens to talk. Beat: horror; the stakes turn mortal.

chapters.title: One Tide Left
chapters.summary: Sable, POV: with one tide remaining before the channel dies, Sable lays out the truth to crew and Odile alike — the money, the murders, Halloway's cover-up. They vote to go on, not for gold but for the drowned diver and the stolen families. Beat: conviction forged.

chapters.title: Night Run
chapters.summary: Sable, POV: a moonless night run through water she navigates by memory and sound alone, Brannigan's boats running shotgun. The river nearly takes them at the Devil's Elbow. Beat: transcendent focus, captain and river as one.

chapters.title: Cutter Bend
chapters.summary: Sable, POV: they arrive at the wreck as Vane prepares to dynamite the hold open. Confrontation on the water; Halloway, arriving by launch, arrests no one — he means to bury everything. Beat: all forces converge.

chapters.title: The Hold Floods
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs: Vane detonates early; the explosion breaches the wreck and traps his own divers. Sable dives into the collapsing hold to pull out survivors while the current tears at her. Beat: sacrifice without hesitation.

chapters.title: Deep Water Justice
chapters.summary: Sable, POV: Vane drowns trying to flee with a strongbox; Halloway moves to seize the recovered funds as 'government property.' Sable scuttles the cutter's remaining hold in deep water beyond anyone's reach — then hands Halloway the ledger evidence Juno kept, forcing an inquiry. Beat: justice outside the law, exacted.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: Juno, POV: weeks later, the inquiry returns the funds' value to the original families; Halloway is quietly reassigned, Odile sails north with a fair-share contract, and Juno takes work mapping the river honestly. Beat: restitution and quiet vindication.

chapters.title: Miles and Years
chapters.summary: Sable, POV: repaired and refloated, the boat runs downstream at dawn. Tam asks where next; Sable realizes she no longer measures life in miles escaped but in seasons returned to. She signs on as the river's pilot-in-residence at Corlow. Beat: belonging, chosen at last.
